hypotheses.text: Exact-duplicate pixel vectors are repeated in data.csv; random train_test_split puts identical images in both train and test, inflating accuracy. Grouping by exact feature hash removes leakage.
hypotheses.predicted_signature: controlled accuracy drops >>5pp below 96% (e.g., to ~80-85%) while claimed stays ~96% on same seed

hypotheses.text: Near-duplicate / same-source images leak: random split overestimates vs source-grouped split, but exact-hash grouping only partially corrects.
hypotheses.predicted_signature: exact-hash controlled drops modestly (2-5pp) but clustered/near-duplicate grouping would drop further

hypotheses.text: Null: rows are i.i.d. images with no duplicates; random vs grouped split are equivalent and 96% is genuine generalization.
hypotheses.predicted_signature: controlled accuracy ~= claimed accuracy within ~2pp (~94-97%) on same seed

hyp.broken_assumption: Random 25% row split equals independent-image split: no identical pixel-vector image appears in both train and test.
hyp.code_patch:
def controlled_eval(df, seed):
    import train
    import pandas as pd
    f = train.feats(df)
    groups = pd.factorize(df[f].apply(lambda r: tuple(r.values), axis=1))[0]
    tr, te = train.split_idx(df, seed, groups=groups)
    y_true = df[train.TARGET].to_numpy()[te]
    y_pred = train.fit_predict(df[f].iloc[tr], df[train.TARGET].iloc[tr], df[f].iloc[te], seed)
    return (y_true, y_pred)
